[[File:Colliding Fermions; Atomic Clock Accuracy (5978323607).jpg|thumb|upright=1.3|NIST physicist Jun Ye adjusts the laser setup for a strontium atomic clock in his laboratory at JILA in 2009.]]
'''Jun Ye''' ({{lang-zh|s=叶军|p=Yè Jūn}}; born 1967) is a Chinese-American [[physicist]] at [[JILA]], [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]], and the [[University of Colorado Boulder]], working primarily in the field of [[atomic, molecular, and optical physics]].

== Education and career ==
Ye was born in Shanghai, China, shortly after the beginning of the [[Cultural Revolution]]. His father was a naval officer and his mother an environmental scientist. He was primarily raised by his grandmother.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Jun Ye {{!}} JILA Science|url = https://jila.colorado.edu/faculty/jun-ye|website = jila.colorado.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-date = June 15, 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170615005520/http://jila.colorado.edu/faculty/jun-ye|url-status = dead}}</ref> Ye graduated with a bachelor's degree in physics from [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] in 1989. He then moved to the [[United States]] to commence graduate studies, completing a master's degree at the [[University of New Mexico]] under [[Marlan Scully]] in theoretical [[quantum optics]] in 1991. He also gained experience in experimental physics under John McInerney working on [[Laser diode|semiconductor lasers]], and spent a summer at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" />

Ye then went to the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] to begin a Ph.D. in physics. He was accepted as the last graduate student of eventual [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prize]] laureate [[John L. Hall]]. His thesis was on high-resolution and high-sensitivity molecular [[spectroscopy]], which he completed in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|title = John Hall's JILA Home Page|url = https://jila.colorado.edu/hall/people.html#students|website = jila.colorado.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150516011015/http://jila.colorado.edu/hall/people.html#students|archive-date = May 16, 2015|url-status = live}}</ref> He then moved to [[California Institute of Technology]] as a Milikan Postdoctoral Fellow, working under [[H. Jeff Kimble|Jeff Kimble]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Quantum Optics: Past Members|url = http://quantumoptics.caltech.edu/past_members.html|website = quantumoptics.caltech.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190409144951/http://quantumoptics.caltech.edu/past_members.html|archive-date = April 9, 2019|url-status = live}}</ref>

Ye moved back to Boulder and [[JILA]] as a JILA Associate Fellow and [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|NIST]] physicist in 1999. John Hall donated most of his lab space to him.<ref name=":0" /> He was promoted to full Fellow in 2001 and has been there since, establishing a research program in [[Atomic, molecular, and optical physics|AMO physics]] and [[precision measurement]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Ye Group|url = http://jilawww.colorado.edu/yelabs/|website = jilawww.colorado.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015}}</ref>

== Research ==
Ye's research focuses on [[ultracold atom]]s, ultracold molecules, and laser-based precision measurement. In 2018 JILA reported that the 3D quantum gas clock reached a frequency precision of {{nowrap|2.5 × 10<sup>−19</sup>}} over 6 hours.<ref>{{cite journal
 |title=JILA Team Invents New Way to 'See' the Quantum World
 |author1=Laura Ost
 |journal=JILA
 |date=March 5, 2018
 |url=https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2018/03/jila-team-invents-new-way-see-quantum-world
 |access-date=March 30, 2017
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190517092816/https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2018/03/jila-team-invents-new-way-see-quantum-world
 |archive-date=May 17, 2019
 |url-status=live
}}</ref>

Such clocks could potentially be used for research into variations in the [[Gravity of Earth|Earth's gravitational field]], searching for particles of [[dark matter]], performing [[Quantum simulator|quantum simulations]] of [[Many-body theory|many-body physics]], and investigating the fundamental nature of [[light]] and [[matter]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title = About Time {{!}} JILA Science|url = http://jila.colorado.edu/news-highlights/about-time|website = jila.colorado.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-date = September 19, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150919105141/https://jila.colorado.edu/news-highlights/about-time|url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = The most accurate clock ever built only loses one second every 15 billion years|url = https://www.theverge.com/2015/4/22/8466681/most-accurate-atomic-clock-optical-lattice-strontium|website = The Verge|date = April 22, 2015|access-date = November 26, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180127084115/https://www.theverge.com/2015/4/22/8466681/most-accurate-atomic-clock-optical-lattice-strontium|archive-date = January 27, 2018|url-status = live}}</ref> He also conducts research on strontium for experiments in [[quantum information science]] (collaborating with [[Mikhail Lukin]], [[Ana Maria Rey]], [[Peter Zoller]], and others).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title = Research {{!}} Ye Group|url = http://jilawww.colorado.edu/yelabs/research/research|website = jilawww.colorado.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-date = November 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125230921/http://jilawww.colorado.edu/yelabs/research/research|url-status = dead}}</ref>

== Popularization of science ==
Ye appeared in the 2018 Netflix documentary [[The Most Unknown (film)|''The Most Unknown'']]<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Most Unknown (2018) - IMDb|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8126390/|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.imdb.com|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310110948/https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8126390/|archive-date=March 10, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> on scientific research directed by [[Ian Cheney]].

==Honors and awards==
Ye has received numerous awards in the field of science, particularly AMO physics. These include:

* the [[Adolph Lomb Medal]] of OSA in 1999
* the [[Arthur S. Flemming Award]] for outstanding federal employees in 2005<ref>{{Cite web|title = GW News Center|url = http://www.gwu.edu/~media/pressrelease.cfm?event_id=5100|website = www.gwu.edu|access-date = November 25, 2015}}</ref>
* the Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Foundation]] in 2006<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile: Prof. Dr. Jun Ye |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrviewhumboldtians%5BpPersonId%5D=1122633&cHash=9703dcdf9ab83fe772f63b4fdfc728aa |access-date=2023-11-01 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de |language=en}}</ref>
* the [[William F. Meggers Award]] of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]] in 2006<ref>{{Cite web|title = William F. Meggers Award – Awards – OSA.org {{!}} The Optical Society|url = http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/meggersaward/|website = www.osa.org|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125203502/http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/meggersaward/|archive-date = November 25, 2015|url-status = live}}</ref>
* the Carl Zeiss Research Award in 2007<ref>{{Cite web|title = Carl Zeiss Research Award|url = http://www.zeiss.com/corporate/en_de/innovation-and-technology/research-award-winners.html#2007|website = www.zeiss.com|access-date = November 25, 2015}}</ref> 
* the [[I. I. Rabi Prize]] in AMO Physics from the APS in 2007<ref>{{Cite web|title = Prize Recipient|url = http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Ye&first_nm=Jun&year=2007|website = www.aps.org|access-date = November 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125194038/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Ye&first_nm=Jun&year=2007|archive-date = November 25, 2015|url-status = live}}</ref>
* five [[Department of Commerce Gold Medal|Gold Medals from the US Department of Commerce]]: for frequency combs (2001),<ref>{{cite web|title=Fifty-Third Annual Honor Awards Program|url=http://hr.commerce.gov/s/groups/public/@doc/@cfoasa/@ohrm/documents/content/prod01_001297.pdf|website=US Department of Commerce – Office of Human Resources Management|access-date=November 25, 2015|archive-date=September 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913025025/http://hr.commerce.gov/s/groups/public/@doc/@cfoasa/@ohrm/documents/content/prod01_001297.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> ultracold molecules (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|title = National Institute of Standards and Technology Recognizes Staff|url = https://www.nist.gov/public_affairs/releases/awards2011.cfm|website = www.nist.gov|access-date = November 25, 2015|language = EN-US|first = US Department of Commerce|last = NIST|date = December 7, 2011|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125211528/http://www.nist.gov/public_affairs/releases/awards2011.cfm|archive-date = November 25, 2015|url-status = live }}</ref> atomic clocks (2014, 2019,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2019-11-14 |title=2019 - Gold Medal Award---Kyle Beloy, David Hume, David Leibrandt, Andrew Ludlow, Nathan Newbury, Jeffrey Sherman, Laura Sinclair, William Swann, Jun Ye |url=https://www.nist.gov/nist-awards/2019-gold-medal-award-kyle-beloy-david-hume-david-leibrandt-andrew-ludlow-nathan-newbury |journal=NIST |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230901190637/https://www.nist.gov/nist-awards/2019-gold-medal-award-kyle-beloy-david-hume-david-leibrandt-andrew-ludlow-nathan-newbury |archive-date=September 1, 2023 |access-date=September 1, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> and 2022<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2022-12-22 |title=2022 - * the 2019 [[Norman F. Ramsey Prize]] of the APS for his ground-breaking contributions to precision measurements and the quantum control of atomic and molecular systems, including atomic clocks<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norman F. Ramsey Prize in Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, and in Precision Tests of Fundamental Laws and Symmetries |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/ramsey.cfm |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=www.aps.org |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181026064456/https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/ramsey.cfm |archive-date=October 26, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

* the Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics in 2021<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Jun Ye receives the 2021 Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/about-springer/media/press-releases/corporate/jun-ye-receives-the-2021-julius-springer-prize/19179300 |access-date=2023-11-01 |website=www.springer.com |language=en}}</ref>
* the Herbert Walther Award from Optica and Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft (DPG) in 2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jun Ye Named 2022 Herbert Walther Award Recipient {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2021/jun_ye_named_2022_herbert_walther_award_recipient/ |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>
* the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] Medal of Honor in 2022
* the Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship from the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] in 2022
* the 2026 [[Wolf Prize in Physics]]<ref>[https://wolffund.org.il/jun-ye/ Wolf Prize in Physics 2026]</ref>

In 2015, [[Barack Obama|President Obama]] selected Jun Ye to receive a [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Award]] for “sustained extraordinary accomplishment”, citing his work advancing "the frontier of light-matter interaction and focusing on precision measurement, quantum physics and ultracold matter, optical frequency metrology, and ultrafast science."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jun Ye Selected for 2015 Presidential Rank Award {{!}} JILA Science |url=http://jilawww.colorado.edu/news/jun-ye-selected-2015-presidential-rank |access-date=December 20, 2015 |website=jilawww.colorado.edu |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222155704/http://jilawww.colorado.edu/news/jun-ye-selected-2015-presidential-rank |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=Y&year=2015&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=November 25, 2015 |website=www.aps.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054622/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=Y&year=2015&unit_id=&institution= |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]]. In 2011 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title = NIST/JILA Physicist Jun Ye Elected to National Academy of Sciences|url = https://www.nist.gov/pml/div689/ye-051011.cfm|website = www.nist.gov|access-date = November 25, 2015|language = EN-US|first = US Department of Commerce|last = NIST|date = May 10, 2011|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125205132/http://www.nist.gov/pml/div689/ye-051011.cfm|archive-date = November 25, 2015|url-status = live }}</ref> and also named a Frew Fellow from the [[Australian Academy of Science]]. In 2017, Ye was elected as a foreign member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cas.cn/tt/201711/t20171128_4624789.shtml|title=关于公布2017年中国科学院院士增选当选院士名单的公告|date=November 28, 2017|publisher=Chinese Academy of Sciences|language=zh|access-date=November 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191123004136/http://www.cas.cn/tt/201711/t20171128_4624789.shtml|archive-date=November 23, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

He is one of the most highly cited researchers in experimental atomic physics in the world, having according to [[Google Scholar]] a [[h-index]] of 120 ({{as of|2022}})<ref>{{Google scholar id|eifJXIEAAAAJ}}</ref> and being regularly named as a [[Thomson Reuters|Thomson-Reuters]] ([[Institute for Scientific Information|ISI]]) Highly Cited Researcher.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Home {{!}} Highly Cited Researchers|url = http://highlycited.com/|website = Highly Cited Researchers|access-date = November 25, 2015|language = en-US|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120402232219/http://highlycited.com/|archive-date = April 2, 2012|url-status = live}}</ref>

Ye also holds four [[United States patent law|U.S. Patent]]s for frequency combs and laser technology.
